title: wringer.workerdiagnosis.v2
description:
A ROUTING DIAGNOSIS ABOUT THE WORKER'S TURN, NEVER A VERDICT. Why the last worker turn produced nothing, read out of the turn's own ledger — and nothing that reads this file may let it reach a verdict: not acceptance's receipts, not vacuity, not health. The same boundary `diagnosis.schema.json` carries, for the same reason.

WHY v2 EXISTS. v1 knew ONE face, `turn_changed_nothing`, and a turn wearing it has always finished: it has a `stopReason`, and a ledger that counted its writes and its refusals. So v1 made those three fields REQUIRED, which was true of everything it could describe. On 2026-08-21 a product manager's run met the other ending — the agent REFUSED the turn — and it fits nowhere in v1: its `face` enum is closed, the file is frozen, and a refused turn never reached `stopReason` at all. Law 7: the enum could not be widened and a required field could not be made optional, so this is a new file and v1 keeps every byte it published.

WHAT CHANGED, exactly: `face` gains `turn_refused`; `stop_reason`, `files_written` and `refusals` move from required to optional. Nothing else moves, and a v1 record is a valid v2 record.

ABSENT rather than null, throughout. A reader that finds no `files_written` knows nobody counted — the turn died before there was a ledger to read. A reader that finds `0` knows somebody counted and the answer was none. Defaulting the first to the second is how a diagnosis starts inventing facts about a conversation that did not happen.

A SIBLING file in the loop bundle, beside `manifest.json`, on the `usage.json`, `vacuity.json` and `diagnosis.json` precedent. It is NOT a face on `wringer.diagnosis.v1`: that schema's `face` is closed too, and its required `gate` and `evidence` are read off a failing gate's log by `gates.cite`. These facts come from the worker's ledger and name no gate.

face.description: Which shape the turn wore. A CLOSED enum, derived from `diagnose.WORKER_FACES` — a face with no name is a face no reader can route on. `turn_changed_nothing`: the turn ended cleanly, wrote no file and raised no refusal. `turn_refused`: the turn ended in an error instead of ending at all — the agent refused the prompt or the session failed. The two are exclusive by construction, one per detector, and the second was added because its absence was the defect: a refused turn used to produce no record of any kind, so the loop's most common real failure was the one ending nothing could describe.

description.description: The hint, addressed to a person, phrased as the possibility it is. From `diagnose.WORKER_DESCRIPTIONS`, so the record and the console cannot disagree about which sentence they carry. `turn_refused`'s names AUTHENTICATION as the most common cause, and names it as a possibility rather than a finding: the hint tier may read text and may never claim. A hint that omits the measured cause because naming it would be a guess is not caution — it is the silence a product manager could not act on.

remedy.description: What the operator can actually do. A POINTER, never a list of credentials. `turn_changed_nothing` names `run.worker.acp.env_passthrough` as the operator's channel and NEVER which variables belong in it: that field exists so a secret crossing into a worker is a declared act by the person who owns it. `turn_refused` names the agent's OWN login and the worker log, because a coding agent authenticates on its own account — Wringer's API key is not its credential and does not reach it, which is measured and is why no remedy here suggests setting one.

stop_reason.description: The ACP `stopReason` the agent reported for the turn — a FACT from the ledger, recorded and never obeyed. A turn claiming `end_turn` having written nothing is the shape a deprecated adapter's unauthenticated reply has. OPTIONAL as of v2, and absent for `turn_refused`: a turn that was refused never reached a stop reason, and `"none"` or `"unknown"` written here would be an invented fact about a conversation that did not happen.

files_written.description: How many files the turn wrote through the file seam. OPTIONAL as of v2: present when a ledger survived the turn, absent when the failure came before there was one. Zero is what makes `turn_changed_nothing` apply; the number is recorded rather than the fact, so a reader sees what was counted.

refusals.description: How many writes the file seam refused during the turn. OPTIONAL as of v2, for `files_written`'s reason. Zero, likewise: a turn that was refused a write DID try to do something, and is a different ending with its own evidence.

engine_words.description: The agent's own last account of itself, if it gave one, carried verbatim BESIDE the description rather than parsed into it. Detection never reads this — F6's law: route on facts, hint on text, claim on neither — and the deprecated adapter's empty success is precisely why text cannot be trusted here. For `turn_refused` this is the agent's error message, and it is the one line that told a real operator what had gone wrong; it is scrubbed by the bundle's redactor on the way to disk like every other write.
